rows.text: The Assembly's item of 23 July 2012 states that Lord Fakafanua was elected after King Tupou VI revoked his predecessor Lord Lasike's position as Speaker, that 'following the appointment of a Speaker, it must then be endorsed by the King', and that 'He was officially APPOINTED by his Majesty King Tupou VI as the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly last Thursday, July 19th.'
rows.uncertainty: The only source that dates the royal appointment; the instrument was not seen and no effective date or clock time is given. The Assembly's own Tongan item created at 17:23 on 19 July still described the appointment as to follow (to_fakafanua_royal_appointment_pending_20120719); both can be true only if the appointment followed later that day.

rows.text: The same item reports that Lord Fakafanua 'started in his new role as the Speaker of the House this morning' (Monday 23 July 2012), thanking members of Parliament for their trust, and that Prime Minister Lord Tu'ivakano congratulated him that morning on behalf of the Cabinet.
rows.uncertainty: His first day presiding after an appointment the same item dates to 19 July. It is a separate claim and is not used as the holder's start, because the source dates the appointment earlier.
